$comment: Build input, not documentation. The rule is TRD Section 7: a component is client-only if its public props include a function, or if it uses state, effects, refs, or browser APIs internally. Everything else is server-capable and carries NO directive. check-client-boundary.mjs fails on any exported component missing from this file, so a new component cannot ship unclassified.
rule: client if public props include a function, or it uses state/effects/refs/browser APIs; else server

special.Table: Static parts are server-capable; interactive parts (sort, select, resize) are client.
special.Alert: Client-only as built: Alert takes `onDismiss`, a function prop, which TRD Section 7 makes the boundary test. A non-dismissible Alert would be server-capable, and it stays ONE component for the reason Tag does - splitting moves the choice into the consumer's import statement.
special.ClaraProvider: Client-only: resolves the system colour-scheme preference in an effect, and holds context state.
special.ButtonGroup: Client-only: roving tabindex needs state and a DOM effect (US-01M0GM3S AC1).
special.Field: Client-only, reclassified during implementation: Field renders a context Provider, and a Server Component cannot - so it and every control reading that context are client-only. The context object itself lives in lib/, not components/, because it is infrastructure rather than a component and does not belong in this classification.
special.Checkbox: Client-only: `indeterminate` is a DOM property that must be set in an effect.
special._overlay: `overlay: true` marks a component that renders a surface floating above the page. check-overlay-contract.mjs requires every BUILT overlay to render through ClaraPortal and to take its stacking from a layer token. Without it, US-01M0GM61's portal is a mechanism nothing obliges anyone to use - which is verbatim the defect D0087 records about the z-index scale.
special.Tag: Client-only, reclassified during implementation: AC2 requires a remove control, so Tag takes `onRemove` - a function prop. Kept as ONE component rather than a server Tag and a client RemovableTag, because splitting it would move the choice into the consumer's import statement.
special.Select: Client-only: it holds open state and the activedescendant highlight, which TRD Section 7 makes the boundary test. There is no server-capable variant to split out - a select that cannot open is not a select. `overlay: true` because its listbox floats above the page, so check-overlay-contract requires it to render through ClaraPortal and take the shared layer token (D0105).
